behavior.scenario: A completed Skill has valid frontmatter, safe resources, UI metadata, and a complete routing/behavior/completion contract.
assertions: python3 scripts/quick_validate.py <skill-dir> exits 0 for static structure even when source Git provenance is unavailable
python3 scripts/quick_validate.py <skill-dir> --engineering exits 0 only after contract, metadata, and clean source Git provenance pass

behavior.scenario: A Skill has a broken local reference, invalid contract, unsafe name, or an invalid split manifest.
assertions: Validation returns a nonzero result with a concrete diagnostic
The splitter and gate reject duplicate IDs, leaked split IDs, malformed result IDs, and non-finite scores

behavior.scenario: Validation, evaluation, or a forward test cannot run because a tool, dependency, permission, or external prerequisite is unavailable.
assertions: Do not claim the Skill is stable without the available validator and evidence
Report the failed prerequisite and preserve the gap rather than masking it in SKILL.md
The CLI distinguishes a missing Git prerequisite from a malformed Skill and returns a nonzero engineering result
evidence: SKILL.md: 5. Validate at the right level

behavior.scenario: A candidate is evaluated repeatedly or a held-out release result is submitted twice.
assertions: Selection accepts only a strict improvement and stages a full immutable candidate tree
A repeated holdout record for the accepted run is rejected
Neither selection staging nor holdout silently overwrites the active Skill
Explicit adoption creates a backup and is the only operation that replaces the active Skill

completion.artifact: A validated Skill directory with SKILL.md, required resource navigation, UI metadata when present, tests/skill_contract.json, and explicit Git provenance evidence before distribution.
assertions: The publish-grade validator exits 0
A missing Git repository is reported as unavailable provenance rather than a successful engineering claim
The contract identifies routing boundaries, behavior failures, and completion evidence
No placeholder or broken local reference remains

completion.artifact: An immutable manifest with train/selection/holdout splits, provenance-bound result artifacts, a staged full-tree candidate, and an optional one-time holdout report.
assertions: Train, selection, and holdout task IDs are disjoint
Every split record payload matches the immutable source corpus, not only its ID
The gate rejects wrong manifest hashes, evaluator versions, candidate fingerprints, non-finite scores, and ID mismatch
Holdout is release evidence only and cannot update the active Skill
Adoption retains a backup and is the only active-Skill mutation
